title: React Module 04 Applied Check
description: Apply rendering, reconciliation, key, list, conditional UI, and state preservation concepts to practical React scenarios.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A todo list uses `key={index}` and users can reorder todos. What is the main risk?

options.text: React may preserve state on the wrong item after reordering
The app will not compile because indexes are forbidden
The list will always render twice
CSS classes will disappear

questions.explanation: Index keys track position, not item identity, so reordering can attach state to the wrong row.

questions.prompt: Why are random keys like `key={Math.random()}` harmful?

options.text: They change every render, forcing React to recreate items
They make numbers render as strings
They disable JSX
They prevent arrays from mapping

questions.explanation: Changing keys make React treat existing children as new, losing state and doing extra work.

questions.prompt: Which choices help React preserve the right identity? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Use stable IDs from data as keys
Keep the same component type at a position when preserving state matters
Use keys to intentionally reset state when needed
Generate a new random key on each render

questions.explanation: Stable keys and consistent types preserve identity; changing a key can intentionally reset state.

questions.prompt: A component switches between `<Input />` and `<textarea />` at the same position. What should you expect?

options.text: React treats different element types as different trees
React preserves all DOM state no matter what
React ignores the change
React converts textarea into Input props

questions.explanation: Different element or component types cause React to replace that part of the tree.

questions.prompt: The virtual DOM makes every update free, so render performance never matters.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The virtual DOM helps React organize updates, but rendering still has costs and poor patterns can hurt performance.

questions.prompt: What is a good empty-state pattern for a list?

options.text: Render a helpful fallback when the filtered array is empty
Render nothing and assume users know why
Use duplicate keys for all items
Throw an error when there are no items

questions.explanation: Empty states explain why no list items are visible and improve usability.

questions.prompt: Which conditional rendering choices are appropriate in React? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Early return for loading or error states
Ternary for choosing between two UI branches
Returning `null` when there is intentionally no UI
Mutating the DOM manually in an `if` statement during render

questions.explanation: React conditions should choose what JSX to return rather than imperatively editing the DOM.

questions.prompt: A detail form should reset when selecting a different user. Which approach can be intentional?

options.text: Key the form by `user.id`
Use the same key for every user
Use array index from an unrelated list
Remove all state setters

questions.explanation: Changing a key tells React to treat the form as a new instance, resetting its state.
